_comment: LBNL FDD Chiller-Plant point -> CAMBER Role mapping. The plant has three chillers (_1/_2/_3) and three cooling towers; chiller 1 and tower 1 are the analysed units (the sensor-bias and tower-fouling faults are imposed on unit 1). Maps ONLY the plant-level points the runnable detectors need: chiller kW/ton (power + CHW loop) for chiller_efficiency, and the cooling-tower supply temp + wet-bulb for cooling_tower_approach. The dataset carries NO refrigerant-side points (evaporator/condenser approach, subcooling, superheat), so the refrigerant-side chiller-drift detectors stay synthetic-only -- see docs/VALIDATION.md. Dataset: LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets (CC-BY). NOTE the exported outdoor-temperature columns are swapped relative to the dataset's own inventory, which documents OA_TEMP as dry-bulb and OA_TEMP_WB as wet-bulb. The simulation's tower controller holds leaving water at max(wet-bulb + 8 F, 60 F): on the 210,661 minutes above the 60 F floor, CT_SW_TEMPSPT equals OA_TEMP + 8 to a median 0.28 F but OA_TEMP_WB + 8 only to 6.3 F. OA_TEMP_WB also exceeds OA_TEMP in 97% of rows (a wet-bulb cannot exceed its dry-bulb), and read as labelled the tower would cool water below wet-bulb half the time. So OA_TEMP maps to wetbulb_temp and OA_TEMP_WB to oat. Until 0.82.0 they were mapped as labelled. The 'bypass' faults are on the single three-way valve that lets condenser water bypass the towers (inventory Table 1 / Figure 2), not on a tower.
